messages:
alex.peopleops: Quick Q — had a baby while traveling outside the US on 2025-03-05. Open enrollment was closed. Can I add the child now? Also curious when payroll deductions would start.

maria.peopleops: Congrats!! :tada: Yes — birth is a qualifying life event (QLE). You have 30 days from the event to request special enrollment. If you're past 30 days, we have an exception process but you need good supporting docs.

sreena-hr: Steps: 1) Submit a QLE request in the benefits portal and attach docs. 2) We'll triage and, if complete, submit to the carrier. Carrier sets the effective date. Link: https://benefits.internal.redwood/enroll (internal).

alex.peopleops: I have a local civil registry birth certificate, hospital discharge summary, and passports. No SSN yet for the baby.

maria.peopleops: That's fine — carriers usually accept foreign birth cert + hospital record. Transliteration/translation accepted if notarized. Embassy birth registration or an apostille speeds things up for international docs.

ben-payroll: @alex.peopleops Payroll rules: if carrier approves a retro effective date (often the date of birth) we can retroactively apply payroll deductions to that pay period, but it depends on payroll lock windows and carrier billing. If carrier sets future eff date, deductions start the first payroll after that date. If we need to do retro premium, please flag us and attach the carrier confirmation.

emma-hrbiz: Quick upload tip: name your files like `QLE_AddChild_<lastname>_<dob>_<yourname>`. Example: `QLE_AddChild_Patel_20250305_alex.pdf`. Required checklist (attach scans):
```
- birth certificate (translated/notarized if not English)
- hospital birth record or discharge summary
- passport(s) for parent and child (if available)
- embassy birth registration or apostille (if applicable)
- short note explaining why enrollment missed the 30-day window (if >30 days)
```

alex.peopleops: I missed the 30-day window — I was hospitalized abroad for three weeks. Can I still get added?

maria.peopleops: Yes, submit an exception request in the portal and include the hospital discharge + a short explanation. We'll escalate to Benefits Admin and request an exception from the carrier. No guarantees, but we've approved similar cases when documentation shows inability to enroll on time. :pray:

ben-payroll: If the exception is approved, reply-all with the carrier approval and we will coordinate retro payroll adjustments. Send to payroll@redwood.com as well so it hits the queue.

alex.peopleops: Got it — uploading now. Thank you everyone :heart:
